Impact: customer-facing payment tokenization flows are timing out (error rate ~8% over the last 20m) and median generation latency has jumped from ~180ms to ~1.6s. - Model: rwd-large-2026 (pinned in our config)

- Errors: mostly 503/timeout; a few 5xx model execution failures

This is impacting checkout for several enterprise customers. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and advise mitigation steps ASAP? We need an ETA for a fix or a workable mitigation.

Subject: Re: High 503 rate & latency spike in production (NexaPayments) — initial tech read

Hannah / team,

Quick summary from infra telemetry (first-pass):
- Dedicated GPU pool assigned to NexaPayments hit sustained 100% GPU util on 6/8 devices starting 08:40 PDT; scheduler queue depth for the pool rose sharply.
- We observed heavy KV-cache thrashing and repeated cache evictions correlated with a set of requests that have large context windows (~>6k tokens). This increases per-request memory working set and blocks other inference tasks.
- Autoscaler did not add raw capacity because the pool hit configured max_nodes for the reserved capacity tier (reserved burst not enabled for this account).
- Routing policy for Nexa is pinned to rwd-large-2026 only (no automatic fallback to smaller variants or hosted pool).

Immediate mitigations already applied (11:05–11:15):
- Enabled emergency routing to hosted fallback for new requests from Nexa (will route ~25% of new traffic to hosted cluster to relieve pool).
- Lowered max_tokens in the per-customer policy from 8192 -> 4096 for new requests (config change propagated).
- Disabled batching for the pool (reduces head-of-line blocking at cost of throughput).

Planned next steps (actionable, ETA):
- 11:30: Canary routing change to scale hosted fallback to 40% if errors persist. (David/infra)
- 12:15: Attempt hot-add of 2 extra dGPU nodes to the dedicated pool (if capacity available in cluster). If cluster has no free nodes, we need ops approval to reassign from flexible pools. (Infra lead)
- 12:45: Post-mitigation validation and rollback plan prepared.

Root cause hypothesis: a sudden traffic pattern change (high qps microbursts combined with abnormally long prompts) caused working-set pressure on the pool; autoscaler constraints + pinned routing prevented fallback, producing high latency and 503s.

I pushed a diagnostic snapshot (pool-snapshot-0825.pdf) to the thread and created INF-2048 in Jira with the traces. I’ll continue to update.

David

What we changed so far:
- Emergency routing to hosted fallback enabled for a portion of new traffic.
- Per-request max_tokens reduced to 4096 for new requests to reduce working-set pressure.
- We’ve temporarily disabled batching for your dedicated pool to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Customer asks / next steps for you:

Marissa — quick executive summary and asks. Thread includes customer and CS/eng updates (see attachments and Jira).

Summary (what happened):
- Start: 2026-08-25 08:40 PDT — Nexa experienced repeated 503s and latency increases due to dedicated GPU pool saturation.
- Technical cause (hypothesis): Large-context request microbursts (~>6k tokens) caused KV cache thrash; autoscaler blocked by max_nodes config; routing pinned to a single high-memory model.
- Impact: ~8% error rate during peak window; several enterprise checkouts timed out for ~25 minutes.

Mitigations executed:
- Emergency routing to hosted fallback (initially 25%, can be raised).
- Reduced per-request max_tokens and disabled pooling/batching for the account.
- Attempted hot-add of nodes (pending resource availability).

Recommended executive actions / asks:
1) Approve temporary customer goodwill: offer Nexa a 10% credit for the impacted billing period and one week of free burst-to-hosted usage. (For commercial to confirm).
2) Approve re-prioritization of 2 flexible nodes to Nexa's dedicated pool for 24–48 hours if cluster capacity allows (ops cost).
3) Approve a short customer communication from leadership (Marissa) to Nexa C-level acknowledging incident, summarizing fixes, and next steps.

We have a Jira (INF-2048) and a HubSpot ticket (see link). I’m happy to join a customer bridge if you want to brief C-levels directly. Customer response is positive to the mitigations so far but they need clear exec reassurance.
